text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--The government intends to raise the labour market levy, a tax component to finance employment initiatives, from its current eight percent to 12 percent over the next five years.
--The major banks are blocking the use of the popular Dankort debit card for internet purchases. The banks are unable to earn revenue on such Dankort use, unlike on credit cards.

--The East Asiatic Company (EAC) says it will not halt production in Thailand of the weedkiller Paraquat despite concerns by Danish investors and politicians. There is opposition on ecological grounds to the production and added political objections to EAC's export of Paraquat (banned at home) from its Thai associate to Burma in defiance of an international boycott of the military government there.
--Local authority debt was virtually unchanged in 1996, at 46.2 billion crowns, from 46.1 billion the year before.
--The shift in the French government lessens Danish isolation in the EU where economic co-operation could centre on reducing unemployment.
--The opposition Conservatives pledge to reduce income tax to 40 percent over 10 years, financing the cut by privatising welfare agencies and introducing more payments for services.
--A wider, softer EMU would benefit Denmark, analysts say, because under such circumstances the Euro would be easier for the Danish crown to shadow.
